annotationRationale: The main route uses equality of complex numbers and trigonometric identities to obtain an exhaustive candidate list. The alternative uses unit-circle powers and conjugation, with those concepts kept method-local.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate for complex-number equations; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Independently, a unit-circle root z would satisfy both 1+z-z²+z³=0 and its reversed equation. Subtraction forces z=1, which fails. Thus the answer is 0, choice A. The stem, choices and key agree; no question figure is supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank questions or methods were supplied. The LIVE and AoPS Solutions 2, 3 and 6 casework route is retained with all six candidates. The polynomial ideas in AoPS Solutions 1 and 3 support the retained conjugation route. Solutions 4 and 5 offer equivalent unit-circle constraints, so another route is unnecessary. Solution 1's unsupported assertion about the remaining roots and the nonexhaustive brute-force attempt are not inherited.
review.annotationCheck: Assessing cnm_h099 and supporting it with cnm_h060 fits the main route. Alternative-specific concepts remain appropriately method-local. No inherited shared-method credits are applicable.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate for complex-number equations; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The addition and subtraction formulas give I(x)=sin(2x)(2cos x-1). Its six zeros in the half-open interval are exhaustively listed. The real parts are respectively 2, -2 or 1, exactly as tabulated, so none is a zero of P.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation and AoPS Solution 2 contain this route. The candidate corrects Solution 2's omission of π/2 and 3π/2, adds a derivation and verified table, and uses original explanatory prose. The source-informed-original designation is honest; neither reference is official MAA material.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first move is motivated, the key identity is derived, the interval endpoints are handled correctly, and the table is easy to reconstruct. The nontrivial final row is explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four supplied IDs are used directly. The symbolic sum-to-product identity is explicitly derived from the mapped addition and subtraction formulas, so it needs no separate intermediate-result node.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The accepted exact links for complex equality, unit-circle trigonometry and angle formulas are relevant. The symbolic identity application extends beyond the formula nodes' special-angle exercises.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The accepted narrower F-TF.C.9 and F-TF.A.2 links support formula use and unit-circle values. This method does not prove the formulas or establish the full standards. No US link is supplied for cnm_h099.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: cnm_h099, cnm_h071, cnm_h070 and cnm_h060 accurately describe the written derivation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Since z is nonzero and its conjugate is 1/z, conjugation and multiplication by z³ produce z³+z²-z+1=0. Subtracting f(z)=0 gives 2z(z-1)=0. The sole permissible candidate z=1 has f(1)=2, proving there are no solutions.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 1 and 3 supply the unit-circle polynomial and conjugation ideas. The reciprocal-equation elimination is accurately identified as a further development, rather than attributed as an existing source argument. The third-party basis and reference credit are appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The substitution is motivated, the required power identities are connected to angle addition, and conjugation and division are explained at use. The short contradiction is complete and accessible without calculus.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Polar powers, modulus, conjugate reciprocals and real-coefficient root preservation all occur directly. The actual conjugation identity is demonstrated, satisfying the root-symmetry node's essential requirement.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The accepted exact links for cnm_h098 and cnm_h103 support modulus and conjugate division. No accepted CN links are supplied for the local polar-power or polynomial-symmetry nodes.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: N-CN.A.3 applies through conjugate reciprocals; N-CN.B.4 and N-CN.B.5 support representation and powers only within their supplied narrower scope. Full geometric-operation coverage is not demonstrated. The root-symmetry node has no supplied US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All four immediate IDs fit. The conjugate-polynomial node is justified by explicit root preservation, without assuming unproved information about the cubic's other roots.
